title: Cellular presentation of projectively cofibrant algebra diagrams
statement:
Use the universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the monoidal model category, strict associative unital algebras, free functor $T$, forgetful functor $U$, and transferred combinatorial model structure of [lem-coef-associative-algebra-model-transfer]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a combinatorial biclosed monoidal model category, not assumed symmetric, with cofibrant tensor unit, the pushout-product axiom, and the nonsymmetric monoid axiom defined in [lem-coef-associative-algebra-model-transfer]. Let $\mathcal J$ be a set of generating cofibrations between cofibrant objects. Let $I$ be any small ordinary category. Give $\mathcal M^I$ and $\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal M)^I$ their projective model structures of [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison], meaning objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations and cofibrations defined by lifting against objectwise trivial fibrations. Write $T^I,U^I$ for applying $T,U$ pointwise. For $i\in I$, let $i_!$ be left adjoint to evaluation, with $(i_!P)(j)=\coprod_{\operatorname{Hom}_I(i,j)}P$.

Every projectively cofibrant algebra diagram $A$ is a retract of a diagram $A_\alpha$ obtained by a small ordinal-indexed continuous chain starting at the constant initial algebra $A_0=T(0)=\mathbf1$. Each successor $A_\beta\to A_{\beta+1}$ is a pushout of $T^I(f_\beta)$, where $f_\beta$ is a small coproduct of maps $i_!(a)$ with $a\in\mathcal J$; in particular $f_\beta$ is a projective cofibration between projectively cofibrant $\mathcal M$-diagrams. No symmetry of $\odot$, siftedness of $N(I)$, or assertion about homotopy colimits is assumed.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal M)$ and $\mathcal C=\mathcal B^I$. By [lem-coef-associative-algebra-model-transfer], $\mathcal B$ is combinatorial, hence locally presentable, complete and cocomplete. In particular it has pullbacks. Apply the presheaf clause of [lem-coef-presheaf-local-presentability] with indexing category $I^{\mathrm{op}}$ and value category $\mathcal B$. This gives local presentability of $\mathcal C=\operatorname{Fun}((I^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal B)$, after the canonical identification of the double opposite with $I$. All sets of objects, arrows and attaching maps below are small in the fixed universe; a natural transformation is a compatible family in a small product of small Hom sets, so $\mathcal C$ also has small Hom sets. The projective model structures on the two diagram categories exist by [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison].

source.place: Higher Algebra, proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, printed pp. 500-501, (B′) and (a)-(d); elementary adjunction and lifting details supplied here. Transferred algebra generators: Haugseng Corollary 3.14.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal S=\{T^I i_!(a):i\in\operatorname{Ob}(I),\ a\in\mathcal J\}$. This is a small set. The two adjunctions in the statement give natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(T^I i_!P,B)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(P,UB(i))$. Explicitly, a map $P\to UB(i)$ extends on the summand labelled by $h:i\to j$ using $UB(h)$, and then extends uniquely to the free algebra; conversely evaluate on the identity-labelled summand and restrict to free generators. These operations are inverse and commute with both sides of a square, so diagonal fillers correspond as well. Thus a map $p:B\to D$ has the right lifting property against $\mathcal S$ exactly when every $Up(i)$ has it against $\mathcal J$. Since $\mathcal J$ generates the cofibrations of $\mathcal M$, this means that each $Up(i)$ is a trivial fibration. The transferred model structure of [lem-coef-associative-algebra-model-transfer] identifies these with the trivial fibrations $p(i)$ of $\mathcal B$. By the projective description in [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison], these are exactly the projective trivial fibrations of $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Higher Algebra, proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, printed pp. 500-501, (B′) and (a)-(d); elementary adjunction and lifting details supplied here. Transferred algebra generators: Haugseng Corollary 3.14.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-presentable-cellular-factorization] in the locally presentable category $\mathcal C$, to the small set $\mathcal S$ and the initial map $0_{\mathcal C}\to A$. Obtain $0_{\mathcal C}\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{p}A$ and a small ordinal $\alpha$ with a chain $A_\beta$ ($\beta\leq\alpha$), $A_0=0_{\mathcal C}$, $A_\alpha=Z$, continuous at every nonzero limit. Each successor is a pushout of a small coproduct of maps $T^I i_!(a)$. The same cited statement says that $p$ has the right lifting property against $\mathcal S$; step 2 therefore makes it a projective trivial fibration.

source.place: Higher Algebra, proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, printed pp. 500-501, (B′) and (a)-(d); elementary adjunction and lifting details supplied here. Transferred algebra generators: Haugseng Corollary 3.14.

proof.text: The projective cofibrancy of $A$ says that $0_{\mathcal C}\to A$ lifts against every projective trivial fibration, by the model-category lifting characterization in [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison]. Apply this to $p:Z\to A$ and the square whose top map is $j:0_{\mathcal C}\to Z$ and whose bottom map is $1_A$. The filler $s:A\to Z$ satisfies $ps=1_A$. Hence $A$ is a retract of the chain endpoint $A_\alpha=Z$ as an algebra diagram.

source.place: Higher Algebra, proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, printed pp. 500-501, (B′) and (a)-(d); elementary adjunction and lifting details supplied here. Transferred algebra generators: Haugseng Corollary 3.14.

proof.text: The constant diagram at the initial algebra is initial: there is exactly one component map to each algebra, and these unique maps are natural. The adjunction $T\dashv U$ of [lem-coef-associative-algebra-model-transfer] makes $T(0)$ initial, since $\operatorname{Hom}(T(0),B)=\operatorname{Hom}(0,UB)$ is a singleton. Its displayed free-algebra formula identifies $T(0)$ with $\mathbf1$: biclosedness implies $0\odot X$ and $X\odot0$ are initial, since their Hom sets are Hom sets out of $0$ into the appropriate right adjoint. Thus only the zeroth summand survives. Similarly $T^I$ preserves small coproducts directly: maps from $T^I(\coprod_t X_t)$ to $B$ correspond successively to maps from $\coprod_t X_t$ to $U^I B$, families of maps $X_t\to U^I B$, and families of algebra maps $T^I X_t\to B$. These are precisely the coproduct universal properties of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Applying these bijections to the source, target and structural map gives $\coprod_t T^I i_{t!}(a_t)\cong T^I(\coprod_t i_{t!}(a_t))$. Consequently each pushout from step 3 is a pushout of $T^I(f_\beta)$ with $f_\beta=\coprod_t i_{t!}(a_t)$, as asserted.

source.place: Higher Algebra, proof of Lemma 4.1.8.13, printed pp. 500-501, (B′) and (a)-(d); elementary adjunction and lifting details supplied here. Transferred algebra generators: Haugseng Corollary 3.14.

proof.text: It remains to check the last assertion about $f_\beta$. Evaluation sends projective trivial fibrations to trivial fibrations, by [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison]. Given any cofibration $a:P\to Q$ of $\mathcal M$, a square from $i_!(a)$ to a projective trivial fibration corresponds under $i_!\dashv\mathrm{ev}_i$ to a square from $a$ to its $i$th component, so it has a filler; its adjoint is the required diagram filler. Thus $i_!(a)$ is a projective cofibration. If $P$ is cofibrant, apply this to $0\to P$ to see that $i_!P$ is projectively cofibrant, since $i_!0$ is initial by the same adjunction. A square from a small coproduct of these maps to a projective trivial fibration amounts to one square per summand. Choose their fillers and combine them by the coproduct universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. This proves that $f_\beta$ is a projective cofibration. Apply the identical summandwise filler argument to $0\to\coprod_t i_{t!}P_t$ and $0\to\coprod_t i_{t!}Q_t$: both endpoints are projectively cofibrant, since every domain and codomain of $\mathcal J$ is cofibrant. Empty coproducts give the initial diagram and its identity map. All arguments use only the stated ordinary model structures and adjunctions.
